original_value: A simple and efficient bottom-roller axle intersections approach for judging the omnidirectional mobility of the Mecanum wheel configuration is proposed and proved theoretically. Based on this approach, a sub-configuration judgment method is derived. Using these methods, on the basis of analyzing the possible configurations of three and four Mecanum wheels and existing Mecanum wheel configurations of robots in practical applications, the law determining wheel configuration is elucidated. Then, the topological design methods of the Mecanum wheel configurations are summarized and refined, including the basic configuration array method, multiple wheels replacement method, and combination method. The first two methods can be used to create suitable multiple-Mecanum-wheel configurations for a single mobile robot based on the basic Mecanum wheel configuration. Multiple single robots can be arranged by combination methods including end-to-end connection, side-by-side connection, symmetrical rectangular connection, and distributed combination, and then, the abundant combination configurations of robots can be obtained. Examples of Mecanum wheel configurations design based on a symmetrical four-Mecanum-wheel configuration and three centripetal configurations using these topological design methods are presented. This work can provide methods and a reference for Mecanum wheel configurations design.

result.paraphrase: A simple, efficient bottom-roller axle-intersection method is proposed and theoretically validated for assessing the omnidirectional mobility of Mecanum wheel configurations. On this basis, a sub-configuration judgment method is derived. By applying these methods to an analysis of possible three- and four-Mecanum-wheel configurations and existing robot Mecanum wheel configurations in practical use, the rule for determining wheel configuration is clarified. The topological design methods for Mecanum wheel configurations are then summarized and refined, including the basic configuration array method, the multiple-wheels replacement method, and the combination method. The first two methods can generate appropriate multi-Mecanum-wheel configurations for a single mobile robot based on the basic Mecanum wheel configuration. Multiple single robots can be assembled through combination methods such as end-to-end connection, side-by-side connection, symmetrical rectangular connection, and distributed combination, thereby yielding a wide range of robot combination configurations. Design examples based on a symmetrical four-Mecanum-wheel configuration and three centripetal configurations are presented using these topological design methods. This work offers methods and a reference for designing Mecanum wheel configurations.
